newsitem.title: UK: Kazakhstan debut Eurobond due next week - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan debut Eurobond due next week - dealers.

text.p: Kazakhstan was expected to launch its debut Eurobond early next week, syndicate managers said on Thursday.
Officials at lead manager ABN AMRO Hoare Govett declined to comment on the exact terms of the deal, saying they were still being discussed with the borrower.
But market players said a $200 million three-year issue to yield in the mid-300s basis points over U.S. Treasury notes was expected from the former Soviet republic.
"Kazahkstan has the same ratings as Romania, which launched a three-year deal earlier this year at 305 b.p. over Treasuries," said a syndicate head at a U.S. bank.
"This is now at around 380 b.p. over, but has suffered due to Romania's economic difficulties. Kazahkstan is likely to come below this level, in the mid-300s b.p.," he said.

Russia successfully launched a $1.0 billion five-year debut bond in November. The deal paid a 9.25 percent coupon and was launched to yield 345 b.p. over Treasuries, and it was still trading at this level.
Kazahkstan's Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin said recently the Eurobond would yield about 9.75 to 10 percent.
Kazahkstan was also considering issuing a Samurai bond issue, he said.
The issue follows roadshows in London, Geneva and New York.
In November, international rating agencies Moody's and Standard & Poor's gave Kazakhstan Ba3 and BB-minus ratings respectively for its long-term foreign currency debt.
The S&P rating was the same as the one it awarded to Russia, but the Moody's rating was slightly lower.
